entities.summary:
Chen Tang (c. 50 BCE – unknown), a distinguished military commander and diplomat of the Western Han Dynasty, etched his name into the annals of classical Chinese history through his audacious and strategically pivotal campaign against the Xiongnu chieftain Zhizhi Chanyu. Operating on the fringes of the Han Empire's authority, his actions dramatically reshaped the geopolitical landscape of the Western Regions, securing crucial trade routes and asserting Han dominance over nomadic threats during a period of intense imperial expansion and consolidation. His legacy is inextricably linked with the projection of Han power far beyond its traditional borders, embodying the assertive spirit of Emperor Yuan's reign.

In 36 BCE, Chen Tang, serving as a deputy protector-general of the Western Regions alongside Protector-General Gan Yanshou, masterminded an unauthorized expedition deep into Xiongnu territory. Disregarding imperial mandates for caution, he rallied a formidable force of Han soldiers and allied local levies, numbering around 40,000, to confront Zhizhi Chanyu, who had established a fortified stronghold near the Talas River in present-day Kazakhstan. The ensuing Battle of Zhizhi was a decisive victory for the Han forces, culminating in Zhizhi Chanyu's death and the complete dismantling of his rogue confederation. This audacious campaign not only eliminated a persistent threat to the Han's western frontiers but also demonstrated the empire's capacity for long-range military intervention.
